prompt: A UTF-16 string contains a supplementary scalar value as a high surrogate followed by a low surrogate. A slice keeps only the high surrogate. What remains?

options.text: A lone surrogate, not a well-formed encoding of that scalar value
options.explanation: Correct. Both units are needed; the retained half is not itself a Unicode scalar value.

options.text: The same complete character in fewer bytes
options.explanation: Slicing has lost part of the encoding.
Removing a unit does not convert UTF-16 to UTF-32.

options.text: A valid pair in little-endian order
options.explanation: Endianness changes byte order within units, not the requirement for both units.

workedExample: A surrogate pair divides one supplementary scalar value between two ordered code units. Keeping only one loses information. Some language string types permit lone surrogates internally, but interchange as well-formed UTF-16 requires valid pairing.
